Chasing costs more at Lord's than at Edgbaston — 21.9 runs against 16.8

Across the T20 cricket we hold ball-by-ball data for at these two grounds, sides batting first at Lord's average 157.6 and sides chasing average 135.7 — a 21.9-run gap, one of the hardest grounds on this list to chase at. At Edgbaston the same gap is 16.8 runs (162.3 batting first, 145.5 chasing), a clear edge to batting first.

Lord's scores at 7.361 an over overall against 7.696 at Edgbaston. The chase at Lord's is at its worst through overs 5-8, where it manages just 6.028 an over and loses 0.667 wickets; a first innings there peaks at 8.975 in overs 17-20.

What that means for this fixture: the toss is worth more at Lord's than at Edgbaston, and a chase there that loses an early wicket is in more trouble than the scoreboard suggests. At Edgbaston a side batting second has more room to absorb one.

Small samples — 10 matches at Lord's, 6 at Edgbaston — and drawn from T20 fixtures at those grounds rather than from The Hundred, whose innings is 20 balls shorter. Read them as ground character, not as a forecast. The live model does not use these averages at all: once a ball is bowled it works from the actual over-by-over run and wicket pattern.

Lord's, on this data. The gap between batting first and chasing there is 21.9 runs against 16.8 at Edgbaston. A chase at Lord's is at its worst through overs 5-8, scoring 6.028 an over and losing 0.667 wickets.

Birmingham Phoenix play home matches at Edgbaston, Birmingham; London Spirit play at Lord's, London. Edgbaston scores at 7.696 an over and Lord's at 7.361. Both figures come from T20 fixtures at those grounds — 6 and 10 matches respectively — not from The Hundred, whose innings is 20 balls shorter.
